title: ipomoea trifida
intro: Ipomoea trifida, commonly known as the 'wild potato' or 'cascabela', is a perennial vine native to tropical Asia and Australia. This plant has been used in traditional medicine to treat various health conditions, including fever, cough, and skin disorders, due to its health benefits such as anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial properties. The therapeutic actions of Ipomoea trifida include its ability to reduce fever, alleviate cough, and promote wound healing. The bioactive constituents responsible for its medicinal properties include alkaloids, glycosides, and phenolic compounds, which work together to provide its therapeutic benefits.
